title: Closest Common Group in an Employee Directory
prompt:
Our employee directory is organized into groups. Groups form a tree, and each employee belongs to one group. Given two or more employees, return the closest group that contains all of them, directly or through descendant groups.

Implement `closest_common_group(parent, employee_groups, employees) -> str`:

- `parent` maps every group name to its parent group; the single root maps to `None`.
- `employee_groups` maps each employee name to the group that directly contains them.
- `employees` is the list of employees to look up.

Practice agreement: the group tree is valid and connected, each employee belongs to exactly one existing group, and the query contains at least two distinct existing employees. Return a **group**, not an employee. Do not modify the inputs. No preprocessing interface is required.

| Group | Parent | Direct employees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Company | — | — |
| Engineering | Company | — |
| Search | Engineering | Alice, Bob |
| Platform | Engineering | Carol |
| Sales | Company | Dan |

Queries: `Alice, Bob -> Search`; `Alice, Carol -> Engineering`; `Alice, Carol, Dan -> Company`.

Follow-up for discussion: what changes if a group has multiple parents? Define what “closest” means when several incomparable common groups exist before choosing a representation or algorithm. This follow-up is not part of the executable tree contract.

references.label: Additional first-person SWE report — multiple-parent follow-up (separate role)

background_note: Original MLE reports ask for the lowest common organizational group for multiple employees without publishing an input schema. The two dictionaries, valid-tree assumptions and callable API are local practice conventions. The DAG discussion is corroborated by a separate public SWE candidate report and a brief MLE variant, but neither establishes a unique tie rule, so no invented DAG behavior is tested. It remains distinct from Report Chain rendering/skip-level tasks.

example.reasoning: Engineering is the lowest group that contains both employees through its children.
